The tree, verified
Reconstructed from dump.txt at commit 759fd56: 363 records, 361 hash-matching on the first pass, the two exceptions being export.sh (it contains the delimiter, so its own SHA can't reconcile) and LICENSE (elided by design). The last record needed the dump footer stripped, after which it hashed to a378f35… exactly as stated. Working tree is trustworthy.

0007_menu_item_image_alt_text.sql is already committed — the dump's git status shows only docs/llm/vendor/claude-output.txt modified, so the git add I flagged last session was done.

The build break, diagnosed
TableOrderSurface.razor:248 is @{ int headingIndex = -1; }, and it sits inside the else { code block opened at line 199. Razor is already in C# there, so @{ is a transition out of a context it was never in — RZ1010. The fix is one line: drop the transition and write the bare statement.

The three other @{ sites in the tree are all legal and I checked each one: KitchenBoard.razor:257 inside <section>, TableOrderSurface.razor:642 inside <li>, AdministrationMenu.razor:167 inside <div class="menu-group-body">. Each has an element as its nearest enclosing construct; line 248 has a C# block. That difference is the whole finding, and it is not decidable from text without a Razor parser — so my ruling is that the compiler is the gate and no shadow parser goes into the suite. Writing a second, worse Razor parser to catch a class the real one catches in three seconds is F-59's mechanism with extra steps. F-104 will record that, and record what the verification checklist could not see: brace balance and tag-tree walks have no notion of transition context.

The menu increment
The tree names it itself. §16.4 currently says:

There is deliberately no IMenuItemImageEventLog … the reader arrives with the surface that renders it, exactly as IMenuSectionEventLog arrived with the section editor.

So Stage 4d — the picture's history, and it is the closest-precedent slice available: MenuSectionEventLog.cs is the template line for line, menu_item_image_event already carries all four types with alt_text_changed written since 0007, and ManageMenuItem.razor already has a .record-list history table to sit beside. Planned files: the new reader, one line in OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions, the panel plus a DescribePicture switch on ManageMenuItem.razor, a new MenuItemImageEventLogTests (6 facts, mirroring the section reader's six plus the one only this table has — the history outliving the row a removal deletes), and one wiring fact.

Test arithmetic: 1242 → 1249. Six new integration facts, one wiring fact. MenuWiringTests 27 → 28, counted-class floor 28 → 29 with the new class cited in §16.4. data-label parity holds — three new <td>, three new labels in the same file.

One thing I want to flag before authoring rather than after: I'm deferring browser downscaling a fifth time. The plan calls it the thing that decides whether pictures are usable at all, and it is unverifiable here — no browser, and swapping a file into a DataTransfer before a static-SSR POST is exactly the shape that looks right and silently posts nothing. It wants a session where you can watch it work. Veto me if you'd rather have that than the history panel.

What is done, in the reconstructed tree
The build fix (F-104). TableOrderSurface.razor:248 — @{ int headingIndex = -1; } is now a bare int headingIndex = -1;. The line sits inside the else { block opened at 199, so Razor was already parsing C# and @{ was a transition out of a context it was never in. The comment above it now records the finding and, more usefully, records why the correct and incorrect forms look identical on the line itself: the nearest enclosing construct decides it. My ruling is that no shadow parser goes into the suite — the Razor compiler already executes this rule, and writing a second, worse one is F-59's mechanism with extra steps.

Stage 4d — the picture's history. The tree named this itself; §16.4 said "the reader arrives with the surface that renders it."

MenuItemImageEventLog.cs — new, mirroring MenuSectionEventLog.cs line for line, with one deliberate divergence documented at length: it must not join menu_item_image. A replace deletes the row it replaces and a removal deletes the row outright, so an INNER JOIN returns a history that silently begins at the current photograph and a LEFT JOIN adds a column null on every row but the newest. That is exactly why 0006 declared no foreign key there.
One registration line, the panel on ManageMenuItem.razor rendered whether or not a picture is attached now (the state the surface could not describe before), and a DescribePicture renderer with one arm per event type and no census in prose.
Six integration facts. The sixth is the one that fails on the reader a maintainer writes by reflex.
A second defect, found reading §7 to write the reader (F-105). §7 said attached | replaced | removed and two named biconditionals. 0007 made it four types and three — a full slice ago. F-77's shape for the seventh time, in the paragraph three sections above the one that legislates against exactly this for the item log. Corrected, the count deleted in favour of a rule, and discharged with something executable: a third fact on MenuEventVocabularyContractTests asserting every type the migration admits has a sentence on the surface that renders it. Its subject is the surface rather than the write service because those four constants are private and widening an API for a test's convenience is the wrong trade — and because §11.4 falls back to the raw string by design, so a missing arm throws nothing and shows up only as a cell reading alt_text_changed where a sentence belongs. F-80's symptom precisely.

Verified so far
Tree reconstructed and hash-checked (361 of 363 exact). String-aware brace balance clean on all six edited C# files, proven sensitive by a planted missing brace and proven not to false-positive on braces inside a string. Razor tag walk on both edited components gives findings identical before and after — the four on TableOrderSurface are the known generic-in-markup artefacts. data-label parity: ManageMenuItem now 6 cells / 6 labels, 8 pages above the floor of 7. Directive gate clean over 51 components. The new vocabulary gate reports zero on the edited tree and all four types against the pristine surface, and I proved the regex loosening is behaviour-preserving for the existing fact (same migration, same eight types) and that FlashFor's "picture-removed" => cannot satisfy an arm.

Arithmetic so far: 1242 → 1250. Six integration facts, one wiring fact, one vocabulary fact. MenuWiringTests 27 → 28, MenuEventVocabularyContractTests 2 → 3, counted-class floor 28 → 29.

Still to do
Changelog v1.39, Appendix A rows (F-104, F-105, Stage 4d), DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, the Stage 4d section in MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, the Slice 54 entry in BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md — then the spec-version and Markdown-table gate simulations, and the archive.

Your build error
TableOrderSurface.razor:248 was @{ int headingIndex = -1; } inside the else block that renders the grouped menu — where Razor is already parsing C#. @{ is the transition from markup into code, so writing it with no markup to leave is RZ1010. It is now a bare statement.

The part worth keeping is why it fooled the verification: there are three other @{ blocks in this tree, all correct, and all four sit after a closed element at the same indentation. What separates them is the nearest enclosing construct — <section>, <li>, <div> for the legal three, else { for this one — and that is not visible on the line. My tag-tree walk and brace-balance checks both passed on the broken file, because neither has any notion of transition context.

No gate added, and I've recorded that as a ruling rather than an omission: markup-versus-code context isn't decidable from text without a Razor parser, csc already decides it in three seconds naming the file and column, and a second implementation in the suite would be two parsers for one rule with the worse one blocking.

Menu progress: Stage 4d, the picture's history
§16.4 had named this slice since Slice 51 — "the reader arrives with the surface that renders it." menu_item_image_event had three slices of writes and four event types and nothing that could read it.

The one design decision worth your eye: the reader must not join menu_item_image. That row is usually gone — a replace mints a new identifier and deletes the old so Cache-Control: immutable stays truthful, and a removal deletes it outright. An INNER JOIN returns a history that silently begins at the current photograph, reads like a complete history, and throws nothing. 0006 declared no foreign key there for exactly this reason; the sixth integration fact now asserts it rather than trusting the comment.

The panel renders whether or not a picture is attached now, since no picture now, three previously is the state the page couldn't describe. No CSS — .manage-subheading was already declared and already used by ManageSitting.razor.

§7 described the table as attached | replaced | removed with two biconditionals. It's four and three since 0007. Three sections above it, §7 says in bold that menu_item_event's vocabulary is not counted in prose anywhere — a rule written after F-77 and then not applied to the next table. Corrected, count deleted, and discharged with a gate, because a corrected sentence is worth nothing when the next migration is written by someone who hasn't read it.

This is the vetoable part. Reversion instructions are in _CHANGES.md; the §7 correction stands either way and the count drops to 1249 with the floor back at 28.
